name: The Wave Organ
blurb: A 1986 Exploratorium sound sculpture at the end of the Marina jetty. Pipes run down into the bay and gurgle and hum as the water moves, and the benches are carved granite from an old cemetery.
tip: Best around high tide. About a 15-minute walk out past the St. Francis Yacht Club on an uneven path.

name: Equator Coffees, Fort Mason
blurb: Marin-roasted specialty coffee at the Fort Mason gate, with Bay views. It sits on the waterfront walk from the Wharf to the Palace of Fine Arts.
tip: Opens 7am on weekends. Small inside, more seating outside.

name: Presidio Tunnel Tops
blurb: 14 acres of park built over the Presidio Parkway tunnels: lawns, a bridge-view overlook and the Field Station curiosity lab, about 10 minutes' walk from the Yoda Fountain.
tip: Free and open daily. Food trucks nearby keep seasonal hours.

name: Earth Wall (Goldsworthy)
blurb: A ball of eucalyptus branches set into a rammed-earth wall in the Presidio Officers' Club. Free history galleries inside cover the Ohlone, Spanish and US Army eras.
tip: Public viewing Saturdays only, 11am–4pm. That's your Saturday.

name: Spire (Goldsworthy)
blurb: A 90-foot spike of 37 cypress trunks in a young forest by the Presidio golf course, scorched by a 2020 fire. Goldsworthy's first Presidio work, and a short walk from Wood Line.
tip: Take the Bay Area Ridge Trail from Arguello Blvd rather than cutting through brush.

name: Presidio Golf Course
blurb: An 1895 Army-era course through eucalyptus and cypress, public since the 1990s. A driving range and clubhouse bar if a full round is too much.
tip: Book tee times online. Dress for wind and fog.

name: Arsicault Bakery
blurb: A tiny Inner Richmond counter often named the city's best croissant. Get the plain or almond croissant and a kouign-amann.
tip: Opens 8am, no seating, sells out by early afternoon.

name: Fort Point
blurb: A Civil War-era brick fort built directly under the south arch of the Golden Gate Bridge. Climb to the roof and look straight up at the deck.
tip: Closed Tue and Wed; open Thu–Mon 10–5. Free.

name: Eagle Point labyrinth
blurb: A short spur off the Lands End trail to a rock point facing the Golden Gate, where a stone labyrinth gets rebuilt every few years. The view of the bridge mouth is the reason to go.
tip: The stones may not be laid out right now. Stairs on the way back up.

name: Sutro Heights Park
blurb: Adolph Sutro's old hilltop estate above the baths: a garden, a lion statue, house foundations and a stone parapet looking straight down Ocean Beach. Few people find it.
tip: Free and open all day. Five minutes uphill from the baths.

name: Lincoln Park Golf Course
blurb: A hilly par-68 city course next to Lands End. The 17th tee looks across to the Golden Gate Bridge, which is rare for a public course anywhere.
tip: Nonresident rate about $70 Fri–Sun. It's steep, so take a cart.

name: Green Apple Books
blurb: A sprawling independent bookstore on Clement St, open since 1967. Creaky floors, handwritten staff picks, a big used section and a good cookbook shelf.
tip: Open 10am–9pm daily. Clement St is also a dumpling and bakery strip.

name: Pizzetta 211
blurb: A tiny Outer Richmond pizzeria making thin, blistered pies from a short menu that changes often. The farm-egg pizza is a regular. A quieter counterpoint to Tony's.
tip: Very small, so expect a wait at peak times.

name: Bison Paddock
blurb: Bison have lived in Golden Gate Park since the 1890s, and a small herd still grazes here off JFK Drive. An odd, peaceful stop near Ocean Beach.
tip: Walk the fence to the back side for the best views.

name: Beach Chalet
blurb: A 1925 building at the west end of Golden Gate Park with WPA-era murals downstairs and a brewpub upstairs looking over Ocean Beach.
tip: Reserve a window table. Come for the view and the murals.

name: Equator Coffees, Hwy 1
blurb: A surfboard-lined Equator cafe on Shoreline Highway, right where you turn off toward Muir Woods. Single-origin pour-over or the shakerato before the drive up.
tip: Opens 6:30am. Last good coffee and pastry before the redwoods.

name: The Pelican Inn
blurb: A Tudor-style English pub a short walk from Muir Beach, with a real fireplace, a ploughman's lunch, fish and chips and pints. Right for a foggy November day.
tip: Opens 11am daily. Fits between Muir Woods and the overlook.

name: Bay Model
blurb: A 1.5-acre working hydraulic model of the entire Bay and Delta, built by the Army Corps of Engineers in the 1950s to simulate tides before computers could.
tip: Closed Sun and Mon, so it won't fit Sunday's drive. Note for next time.

name: Waldo Point houseboats
blurb: Sausalito's floating neighborhood of hand-built, often eccentric houseboats. Otis Redding wrote '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' while staying here.
tip: Park on Gate 5 Rd and stay on the public walkways. The docks are homes.

name: Bar Bocce
blurb: A waterfront pizza bar on Bridgeway with fire pits and heaters on the sand. Crisp seasonal pies, salads and spritzes while boats drift past.
tip: Reserve on weekends. Dogs welcome outside.

name: Blue Bottle, Ferry Building
blurb: Blue Bottle's flagship kiosk inside the Ferry Building, four minutes from the Hyatt. A New Orleans iced or a pour-over on the bayside benches.
tip: Opens 6:30am. Lines peak around 8:30.

name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
blurb: Tomales Bay oysters, clam chowder and grilled cheese at a marble bar facing the Bay Bridge. The best sit-down lunch near QCon.
tip: Get there at opening (11:30) or after 2 to skip the line.

name: Ferry Plaza Farmers Market
blurb: CUESA's market outside the Ferry Building: Northern California produce, mushrooms, citrus and ready-to-eat stalls. The cook in the pair will want to browse.
tip: Tue and Thu 10am–2pm, Sat 8–2. Easy on a QCon lunch break.

name: Boichik Bagels
blurb: New Jersey-style bagels with a big following. Try the pumperthing or lox and schmear, six minutes' walk from the Hyatt.
tip: Opens 6:30am, closes 1:30pm. Order ahead online.

name: Tadich Grill
blurb: Open since 1849 and often called California's oldest restaurant. White-jacketed waiters, a long wooden counter, cioppino and petrale sole.
tip: Mon–Fri 11–9. Counter seats usually open without a reservation.

name: House of Prime Rib
blurb: A 1949 institution where prime rib is carved tableside from silver carts and the salad is spun at the table. A once-per-trip splurge.
tip: Reservations fill weeks out, so book now. Dinner only.

name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
blurb: Tony Gemignani's North Beach pizzeria with ovens for Neapolitan, New York, Detroit, Roman and coal-fired styles. The wood-fired Margherita is limited to a small daily count.
tip: Opens at noon and the line forms before then.

name: Golden Boy Pizza
blurb: Thick focaccia-style Sicilian squares since 1978. Get the clam-and-garlic. Cheap, fast, and a block from Tony's.
tip: Counter only. Eat it in Washington Square.

name: City Lights Booksellers
blurb: Lawrence Ferlinghetti's 1953 Beat bookstore and the publisher of 'Howl'. A poetry room upstairs and three floors of unusual, carefully chosen titles.
tip: Open 10am–10pm, so it works after a North Beach dinner.

name: Vesuvio Cafe
blurb: A 1948 Beat-era bar across Jack Kerouac Alley from City Lights, with a stained-glass mezzanine and decades of ephemera on the walls.
tip: Grab a mezzanine seat by the window.

name: Caffe Trieste
blurb: Opened in 1956 and said to be the first espresso house on the West Coast; Coppola reportedly wrote much of The Godfather here.
tip: Open 7am–10pm. Bring some cash.

name: Liguria Bakery
blurb: A family bakery on Washington Square since 1911 that makes only focaccia, wrapped in white paper and tied with string.
tip: Tue–Sat 7am to noon or sellout. Morning only.

name: Fortune Cookie Factory
blurb: A one-room shop in Ross Alley where cookies are folded by hand off a small press. You can have custom fortunes baked in.
tip: Open 9am–7pm. Small cash; they ask a fee for photos.

name: The Buena Vista
blurb: Where Irish coffee arrived in the US in 1952. Bartenders build a dozen at a time in a row of stemmed glasses, three minutes from the hotel.
tip: Opens 8am weekends. Mornings and late evenings are calmer.

name: Saint Frank Coffee
blurb: The best specialty coffee within reach of the hotel: direct-trade beans and careful pour-overs in a bright Polk St cafe. Try the flight.
tip: Open 7am–6pm. Seats fill with laptops, so take it to go.

name: Square Pie Guys
blurb: Crispy-edged Detroit-style pizza near Ghirardelli Square. An easy, good-value dinner on nights you skip North Beach.
tip: Order at the kiosk. Open until 10:30pm Fri–Sat.

name: USS Pampanito
blurb: A WWII submarine you walk through bow to stern, moored next to Musée Mécanique. Torpedo rooms, bunks and the engine room.
tip: Open 10am–6pm, about $25. Single-file inside, so go early.

name: Swan Oyster Depot
blurb: A 1912 seafood counter with about 18 stools. Sicilian sashimi, cracked Dungeness crab, oysters, and banter that's half the experience.
tip: Mon–Sat 8am–2:30pm. Arrive at opening. Long known as cash only.

name: Emporium Arcade Bar
blurb: Three levels of pinball, Mortal Kombat, Time Crisis and skee-ball inside the restored 1926 Harding Theater, with a full bar. The gamer night out.
tip: 21+. $10 buys 40 tokens. Opens 4pm weekdays.

name: Real Guitars
blurb: A long-running shop of vintage and used guitars, basses and amps, curated with no junk. Staff let you plug in and play.
tip: Mon–Sat 11–5. Tucked on an alley off Mission near 11th St.

name: Lombard Street (crooked block)
blurb: The one block between Hyde and Leavenworth with eight hairpin turns, built in 1922 because the 27% grade was too steep to drive straight down. Hydrangeas line the switchbacks, and the top looks out over the bay to Coit Tower.
tip: About a 7-minute walk uphill from the hotel. Go early morning or after dark to beat the crowds. Stairs run down both sides, and the Hyde St cable car stops at the top.
